title: You guys interested in earnings reports at all? I built a system around them.
author: TheObserverDev
selftext:
>I built a system that scores every earnings report. Here are the rules:

* An AI reads the company’s report (only the report, no stock price, no news) and gives it a score from 0 to 100: sales growth, margins, cash, and what the company says about the next quarter.
* The score is compared with the company’s own last 8 reports (2 years), so you can see if the business is getting better or worse.
* Separate from the score, each stock gets a grade from A to F for cheap or expensive at today’s price.
* To make the list at all, the stock has to be up at least 25% over 1 year and 130% over 5 years, and trade enough every day.
* Bots buy at the close of the first market day after the report, never on report day, to skip the first swings.

Does it work? I tested it on about 500 S&P 500 reports from July to September, after the AI’s training cutoff, so it couldn’t know what happened next. The highest scores beat the lowest by about 7 points after 40 market days. By 60 days the edge was gone. One season, so it’s a first signal, not proof.

Is this something you’d want to see more of? What would you check in a report that I’m missing?      

  
yes, i do make videos with cloude,   and post them in yt,  i'm currently making the mornings earning report and afternoon earning report .      this could help some people or maybe not,  i will say if your strategy is long term.  then this could help you.    i'm still trying ot improve on the output. hope it helps.  give me some tips on how can i improve in the video productions side.  and if you recomend any strategies on long term earning report strategies,  then i will take it to cloude.

comments.author: TheObserverDev
comments.body: if i get at least 15 upvotes, then i will keep posting new updated videos here, uploaded directly, no links.  it takes me few minutes.    like i stated, i'm updating daily the earninggs report and giving them an score.  that's all this is about.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
testing only on reports after the model's cutoff fixes the leak we talked about on your October thread, so that part I'd now trust.

what I'd check next is how many separate bets those 500 reports really are. they all came out in the same ten weeks, so the 40 days after them are mostly the same 40 days of market. if the high scorers lean toward one sector, a 7 point gap could be that sector's quarter and nothing to do with the reports. splitting the gap by sector would show it quickly, and so would counting how many names carry it.

the other one is the entry filter. if up 25% in a year and 130% in five is measured today instead of on each report's date, the list already knows who kept going.

replies.author: TheObserverDev
replies.body:
Ran both checks, thanks. You were right on the first one. The 7 point gap mostly came from tech (27 of the 65 high scores were tech, and tech had a good stretch) plus a few big winners. Compared inside each sector it drops to about +2 to +4, and the luck range crosses zero. So one season, no proven edge yet.

On the filter: it only used prices from before each report, and the score test didn’t use the filter at all. Small correction, the thresholds were 25% and 125%, not 130%. Both tests also use today’s S&P 500 list, so there’s some survivorship bias too.

Next season I’ll run it sector-neutral from the start and post it either way.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: +2 to +4 with the range crossing zero is a real answer, and most people never run the check that takes their own number away. on today's S&P list: for one recent season it's small, only a handful of names left the index since. it grows fast if you ever stretch the test back years.

comments.author: ogb-officials
comments.body: ER is more like a coin flip... How do you really define the edge? A company can have a great report but still flunk after hours, also a company can have bad reports but still bull up

replies.author: TheObserverDev
replies.body:
I aim for 2 years of earnings reports (the last 8) before deciding on a company, not just one. The ranking looks at whether the business keeps getting better over those 2 years.

And you’re right about report day, it’s a coin flip. That’s why my bots never buy on report day, they wait for the next day’s close. When I tested it, the edge showed up over about 2 months, not overnight
